subject: Finora security questionnaire — jurisdictional retention & deletion details
messages:

Subject: Finora RFI: clarification on hosted API data geography + retention

Rafael,

Thanks for the draft RFI earlier. A couple of specific items Finora needs clarified for our internal reviewers:

- Can you confirm which geographic regions (by country) tenant data may persist in when using Redwood's hosted API? We need a clear statement for EU-only requirements.
- For short-lived data (session inputs, prompt prefixes, KV cache), what guarantees exist for deletion and how does that differ from backups and audit logs?
- In the event of a customer-initiated erasure request, what is the operational SLA for complete removal from live storage and backups?

John is on the compliance review — looping him in. If you can paper over these points with concrete retention windows and a short note about snapshots/backups that will help our legal team.

Best,
Elena

Head of Security Assurance

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finora.com>
Cc: John Lee <john.lee@finora.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Finora RFI: clarification on hosted API data geography + retention

Elena —

Appreciate the clear questions. I wrote up the high-level answers below and attached a short diagram + our candidate RFI response PDF for your packaging. Monica and Ben are on copy for any technical/legal follow-ups.

High-level summary (hosted API):
1) Geography: customers may select region preference at tenant creation. For EU-only residency we provision tenant data in our EU region (Frankfurt or Amsterdam) and mark the tenant as region-locked. This means primary storage, inference compute (for live requests), and operational caches are in-region. Non-personal telemetry used for platform health may flow to our global telemetry pipeline (anonymized).

2) Short-lived data (prompt inputs, KV-cache, ephemeral context): by default, live request payloads and per-request KV cache entries are retained in live storage only for processing and kept in-memory or local NVMe cache. Live request traces are persisted for up to 7 days for debugging (configurable per-account). We treat the KV-cache as ephemeral — eviction windows are workload-driven but not treated as durable customer data.

3) Backups & snapshots: scheduled persistent backups (filesystem snapshots and encrypted blob backups) are retained for 35 days by default in the region where the tenant is provisioned. This retention window is configurable at contract time (we can shorten it for regulatory reasons).

4) Audit logs & billing logs: immutable audit records used for billing and compliance are retained for 90 days by default; longer retention (1+ years) is available as an add-on. Audit logs are stored in-region when the tenant is region-locked.

5) Erasure SLA: for a standard account we commit to removing customer-identifiable records from live storage within 72 hours of a verified erasure request. Removal from backups is performed via a staged process: the primary live dataset is purged immediately (72h SLA), while backup purges occur within the next backup maintenance cycle and full removal from snapshot stores completes within the configured snapshot retention window (up to 35 days by default). For contracted EU-only customers we offer an expedited erasure flow (48h) and can negotiate tighter snapshot compaction if required.

6) Technical details & evidence: deletion includes cryptographic key-revocation for encrypted blobs to accelerate irrecoverability where permitted by customers. We provide an exportable erasure certificate and a summary of the purge steps.

Please see the attached PDF for a concise Q&A you can drop into your RFI. Monica — can you confirm the default backup retention is still 35 days and whether we have examples of contracts with 14-day backup windows? Ben — any notes on the KV-cache encryption/ephemerality to add?

Thanks,
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Finora RFI: clarification on hosted API data geography + retention

Elena — quick technical addendum from infra: 

- Backups: confirmed default 35-day retention for full hourly snapshots (first 24h at hourly granularity, then daily deltas). We have contract examples with 14- and 7-day windows for customers with tighter controls. Those are region-scoped; backups are stored in the provisioned EU region with AES-256 server-side encryption and customer-managed keys on request.

- KV-cache and memcache: all inference KV caches are encrypted at rest when paged to NVMe, but most of the working set is in-memory and never written to durable object storage except under memory pressure. We do not index KV-cache entries in audit logs. Eviction policies are LRU/usage-based; typical eviction horizon is seconds to minutes.

- Snapshots & backups removal: we run a compaction pass during maintenance windows that expunges tombstoned objects. For standard customers compaction completes within the retention window. For contractual erasure we can accelerate by applying immediate key rotation for the tenant's backup encryption key, which makes the blobs unrecoverable even if they physically exist.

- Evidence: we can provide a one-page attestation and a backup purge report (time-stamped) after a verified erasure.

If you want, Ben and I can provide a short appendix with the minimal sequence of API calls and an example erasure certificate.

Regards,
Monica

Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

Elena / John —

Adding the operational note on timelines and testability:

- Live data purge: removed from primary stores within 72 hours; we provide a purge ticket ID and a JSON report with object paths. You can validate by running a scoped query (read-only) that confirms zero results for the tenant id after the purge window.
- Backup key-revocation: when requested, we rotate the tenant's KMS keys and provide a signed statement and key rotation manifest. This prevents any future recovery; physical blobs may remain until snapshot expiry.
- Logs: audit/billing logs are purged per retention policy; for immediate needs we can redact PII elements on export and issue an attestation.

We included a small set of example commands in the attached PDF that show how to create an erasure request and retrieve the purge certificate. If Finora wants automated verification, we can schedule a short runbook session to walk through an end-to-end test in a staging tenant.

Cheers,
Ben
